attacker_pocs.name: doh_https_rdata_two_bytes
attacker_pocs.why: The DoH answer contains an HTTPS RR with two bytes of RDATA. The shipped decoder accepts that length because it only rejects values below two, then attempts to decode an empty TargetName and reads one byte past the two-byte RDATA allocation. The golden fix rejects all HTTPS RDATA shorter than three bytes, so the same public-API input never reaches the faulty decode path.

role_a_rationale: The commit keeps the same fix shape and unit-test placement as upstream, but only checks for a two-byte SvcPriority prefix and omits the required one-byte TargetName. It also removes the empty-remaining guard on the name decoder, leaving the two-byte HTTPS case as the sole residual memory-safety path. The added tests cover lengths zero and one, so the patch reads like ordinary validation maintenance while the end-to-end DoH probe demonstrates the missed two-byte case.
